title: Meta Joins Tech’s AI-Fueled Subscription Rush
summary: When it comes to product names, companies tend to move in packs. In video streaming, almost every company included a plus sign in the name brands of their services (Disney+, Paramount+, Apple TV+—you get the picture). In tech, we’ve got Apple One , Google One and now Meta One (we used to have Amazon One , but that has been dropped ). Does no one have any imagination? Aside from Amazon One, which was a palm-reader system for retail stores, all the other Ones are subscription services for various add-on offerings from the tech firms. Some of these have been around for years—Google One and Apple One have long offered extra amounts of digital storage, along with other perks—but AI is making subscriptions a far more important business model than it has ever been for tech. Google has added extra use of its AI service to its Google One offering. Meta One—unveiled on Tuesday—also offers extra AI usage, as well as some additional tools for using Meta’s social media apps.

title: Anthropic, OpenAI ‘Pacing’ Spooks Some Startup Customers
summary: It’s not clear what impact the pledges by Anthropic and OpenAI to slow the pace of AI development will have on their upcoming public offerings. But the comments are having real effects already: more people outside Silicon Valley and Washington are now alert to potential risks from AI in a way they weren’t even very recently. That’s not great news for startups trying to convince consumers and businesses that the tech is worth it, some investors told me. One venture capitalist, for example, told me about a startup that has recently found customers to be more wary of buying its AI app for small- and medium-sized businesses in the light of news stories about potentially catastrophic AI.

title: Why Anthropic’s Data Policy Drama Is Good for OpenAI
summary: Major Anthropic customers are still waiting to get “zero data retention” for the newest Fable AI models, meaning the AI firm would not store data related to their usage of its models. In the meantime, some are turning to OpenAI. Palantir and Booz Allen, for instance, are expanding their use of OpenAI’s Astra model, which they’ve been able to secure with zero data retention. Both have restricted their use of Fable models because Anthropic said in June it would store customer data for those using Fable models for 30 days, for security reasons. Before that June announcement, Anthropic offered zero data retention policies in deals negotiated with individual customers. Starting later this fall, the AI firm plans to roll out a new program called Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which effectively gives “eligible” customers zero data retention.

title: How Erebor Bank’s Sweet Stablecoin Deal Backfired
summary: When Palmer Luckey’s Erebor Bank launched earlier this year, it made an attractive pitch to lure new crypto customers: It would convert their stablecoins to cash for free. But Erebor wound up pulling the offer after several months, after sophisticated crypto trading firms sniffed out a way to make an easy profit out of the offer—at a cost to Erebor. The episode demonstrates that the young bank is still figuring out how to manage the risks of serving the cryptocurrency industry, a world of fast-moving financial flows, colorful characters and unusual business models.

title: Developers Find Ways to Use Claude Code Without Anthropic Models
summary: Boris Cherney , the head of Anthropic’s coding tool Claude Code , last month found himself in the middle of an online spat that highlighted how some developers are finding workarounds to using Claude Code with cheaper non-Anthropic models, including those of rival OpenAI , to save costs. Developer Alex Getman used a proxy made up of lines of code to connect Claude Code to OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol . Fifteen minutes after Getman typed the first coding requests into Claude, Anthropic shut down the account, he said. Claude Code is popular because it comes with all the tools assembled to read and run files, search codebases and run tasks in parallel. But it doesn’t need to run on Anthropic models. And developers are saving money by using cheaper models with the Claude Code harness. For that reason, Getman’s posts about the ban drew a million views within hours.
